inputs.share_count_basis: 144.820m ordinary shares at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 interim report); dilution from share schemes is immaterial and SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so the count is held FLAT. Post-balance-date DRP issuance ($5.0m reinvested Jul-2026, ~0.7m shares) is dividend-in-kind, value-neutral, not modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: NZ$84.1m management net debt at 31-Dec-2025 (borrowings less cash, EXCLUDING lease liabilities - see lease_treatment) + NZ$36.7m deferred acquisition consideration (AUD7.3m/yr instalments Sep-2026..Sep-2030, carried at amortised cost). Dec-2025 rather than the seasonal Jun-2026 peak ($106.7m) is used because year-1 flows are FULL FY2026 including the FY2026 working-capital build; using the Jun-26 balance would double-count the H1-26 WC build. Deferred consideration added because the acquired earnings are fully in the flows.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (net debt anchor; verified against 2026-06-30 interim: mgmt net debt $106.7m seasonal peak, leverage 0.7x)
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, Share-based payments $1.169m (filing in $000s: 1,169). No separate equity-award withholding-tax line disclosed; NZ market, SBC immaterial.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received FY2025 $2.602m NOT stripped: the company carries net DEBT (no material net-cash pile to double-count); flows are unlevered EBITDA-based so interest income is outside the projection anyway.
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. Full lease payment (principal + lease interest, FY2025 $8.464m + $4.740m = $13.2m; ~1.1% of enlarged revenue) is deducted from the flows via lease_cost_pct, and lease liabilities (~$116m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Charging both flows and balance sheet would double-count ~$0.7/share (owner-fcf.md section 7b); this matches the repo convention (3116.T, TPW.AX, 2CC.NZ, TAH.NZ). D&A driver (da_pct) is ex-ROU depreciation ($18.4m FY2025 = 2.05%; ~1.85% on the enlarged base) so ROU depreciation is not charged on top of lease payments.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI (Shelby JV LLC 32.5%, ANZ Exports 15%, Fayman NZ 5%; underlying NCI $15.8m of $77.6m underlying NPAT in FY2025, guidance implies ~$17.5m of ~$75m in FY2026) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a COMBINED cash-tax + NCI leakage rate on EBIT (~36.5% = 1-(1-17% eff tax)x(1-23% NCI share)). NCI equity ($12.9m) is deliberately NOT also deducted in the bridge - charge once (owner-fcf.md 7c). Calibration: year-1 attributable unlevered NOPAT $61.1m = FY2026 guidance NPATAS midpoint $57.5m + ~$3.6m after-tax attributable net borrowing interest.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-27T04:59:43Z (NZX regular close, NZ$7.10; 52w range 4.90-7.20; price is at the top of the range the day after the H1-2026 record result and guidance upgrade)
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10y horizon, per dcf-methods routing (diversified operating agribusiness: Global Proteins / Horticulture / Logistics). ANCHOR IS UNDERLYING, NOT REPORTED: FY2025 reported NPATAS $101.0m includes ~$26.4m group-share one-off non-cash IFRS 3 step-acquisition remeasurement gains ($40.6m pre-tax at group level, in Other income) from revaluing previously-held 50% stakes in Fayman/FIG (+$23.9m) and ANZ Exports (+$2.5m) on obtaining control. Base year is management Underlying: FY2025 Underlying EBITDA $137.6m / Underlying NPATAS $61.8m; year-1 (FY2026) is built to tie to guidance Underlying EBITDA $135-142m and Underlying NPATAS $55-60m (raised 26-Aug-2026 from $50-55m). Year-1 revenue growth of ~55% is CONSOLIDATION of businesses acquired Sep-2025 (Fayman, ANZ Exports, Meateor Australia) plus Esro control - NOT organic; organic growth thereafter 2.5-4.5%. Gross margin fell to 18.9% in H1-2026 (31.3% H1-2025) because the acquired Edible Proteins trading businesses run single-digit EBITDA margins - hence group EBITDA margin ~9.9% on the enlarged base vs ~15% before. FY2026 revenue estimate ~$1,400m built from divisions: Horticulture ~$340m (H1 $223.9m, crop 93% sold), Global Proteins ~$975m (H1 $492.7m), Logistics ~$150m (H1 $74.5m), eliminations ~-$65m.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.5% vs revenue 13.8% / EPS 36.4%: ALL headline CAGRs are distorted - revenue and FCF by the Sep-2025 consolidation of previously part-owned JVs (not organic), EPS by the FY2025 one-off step-acquisition gains and the FY2020 COVID / FY2023 cyclone troughs; equity is depressed by the 50-75% payout policy. None is a usable forward growth rate. Selected 4.5% = year-2 organic base-case growth (Premium apple mix + petfood volumes), fading to 2.5%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - full lease payments): FY2019 29.3, FY2020 18.0, FY2021 12.5, FY2022 18.4, FY2023 35.9, FY2024 29.6, FY2025 60.5. The FY2025 jump is one quarter of consolidated trading businesses plus favourable WC timing - not a clean organic base, which is why the model rebuilds FY2026 from guidance components instead of growing last_fcf.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at guidance (Underlying EBITDA ~$138.6m, NPATAS ~$57.5m; crop 93% sold, so the year is largely locked). Thereafter organic-only growth of 4.5% fading to 2.5% - Premium apple mix (79% of volume, Dazzle/Posy into Asia/Middle East) and structurally growing petfood-ingredient demand - with group EBITDA margin edging from 9.9% to 10.5% as the Global Proteins FY27 $85m divisional target is broadly met and the Esro Petfood drag (-$4m/yr underlying) is stabilised by FY2028. No credit for future M&A: the DCF values the business Scales owns today. NCI leakage held at ~23% of profit, effective cash tax ~17% drifting up 1pt.
scenario_narratives.bull: Premium mix accelerates and prices hold despite Middle East tension; Global Proteins beats the raised $85m FY27 EBITDA target on tight supply economics and the new US fish/poultry JV; Esro is stabilised or exited cleanly and the Netherlands plant adds capacity; bolt-on M&A continues to be value-accretive (captured only via the higher organic path - 7% fading to 3% - and margin reaching 11.5%; buyouts of NCI trim leakage to 35%). Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two live risks crystallise: Esro Petfood losses deepen through 2026-27 and exit/stabilisation costs mount (management still calls the region unstabilised after the ~$20m loan impairment and -$20.3m negative net assets consolidated in H1-2026), and a Gabrielle-class Hawke's Bay weather event hits the FY2027 crop (FY2023 precedent: group NPATAS fell ~90% to $5.2m). Year-2 revenue -6%, margin 7.8% with recovery to only 9.3% as Edible Proteins trading margins compress and freight costs stay elevated; leakage spikes to 42% in the loss year because the weather loss is 100% parent (Horticulture) while NCI-shared Global Proteins profits continue. No further NPATAS growth beyond CPI.

wacc_rationale: Built in NZD for NZD flows, applied identically to all three scenarios (risk priced once - discrete Esro/weather severity lives in the 25%-weighted bear scenario, not in per-scenario discount rates). Components: NZ 10y risk-free 4.4% + beta 0.95 x NZ ERP 5.5% = 9.6% base CoE; +0.5% size/liquidity (NZX mid-cap, ~$1.03bn cap - deliberately modest per market cap); +0.75% weather/cyclicality concentration (Hawke's Bay single-region apple exposure; FY2023 cyclone cut attributable NPAT ~90% - the recurring, systematic component); +0.5% acquisition-integration + live Esro distress (goodwill $40.6m to $172.9m in 18 months, four deals bedding in); +0.25% FX/export/shipping (79% USD crop exposure, geopolitical freight lanes) = CoE ~11.6%. Blending ~13% net debt at ~4.7% after-tax gives WACC ~10.7%; adopted 11.5% - rounded UP into the standard NZ small/mid-cap 11-12% band so the premiums are not diluted by leverage. Not stacked further: bear scenario and weights already carry event severity.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; base scenario; terminal growth capped at 2.0-2.5% for a mature agribusiness.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% (house default 15%) because two named downside risks are LIVE, not hypothetical: Esro Petfood is a consolidated negative-net-asset business management says still needs stabilising after a ~$20m H1-2026 loan impairment, and Hawke's Bay weather concentration has already produced a ~90% one-year earnings wipe-out (FY2023) within the forecast horizon's expected event frequency. Bull trimmed to 25% because it requires several independent successes (GP $85m target, Esro clean exit, Premium pricing through Middle East tension, accretive further M&A).
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapses: SBC is ~0.1% of revenue (NZ market convention, cash-remunerated workforce), so street IV exceeds house IV by only ~NZ$0.11. band_position set to null rather than a degenerate figure; the NZ$7.10 price sits far above BOTH bases.

sanity_check.method: 10y monthly Yahoo closes, Dec FY-end price vs same-FY metrics; SBC-adjusted both sides; FY2023 (Cyclone Gabrielle: GAAP P/E 102x) and FY2025 (step-acquisition gains inflate EPS; EV/EBITDA on reported 169.9m) EXCLUDED from averages, kept in table.

FY2025.excluded: reported EPS/EBITDA inflated by one-off IFRS 3 step-acquisition gains

sanity_check.implied_multiples_note: Implied on FY2025 UNDERLYING NPATAS ($61.8m) and Underlying EBITDA ($137.6m), SBC-adjusted, since reported FY2025 figures carry the one-off gains; P/E on reported (5.7x) shown for completeness. Historical GAAP P/E series is noisy (FY2019 inflated by divestment gains, FY2020-22 EPS depressed) - P/B and EV/EBITDA are the steadier yardsticks.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip: every implied multiple is BELOW its historical average (P/B 1.29x vs 2.10x avg; EV/EBITDA 5.6x vs 10.6x avg) and base upside is negative. The check guards against over-valuation; the finding here is the opposite gap - see valuation_philosophy for why the DCF and the market's multiple disagree.

cross_checks.residual_income: Underlying ROE ~13.9% ($61.8m / $443.6m) vs CoE ~11.6% and g 2% gives warranted P/B = (13.9-2)/(11.6-2) = 1.24x book = NZ$3.83/share - independently corroborates the DCF's NZ$3.95 (1.29x book).
cross_checks.historical_multiple_value: Memo only: FY2026 guidance EBITDA $138.5m at the 10y average 10.6x EV/EBITDA less lease-inclusive net debt + deferred consideration (~$234m) = ~NZ$8.50/share. The gap to the DCF is the price of (a) an 11.5% NZD discount rate vs the single-digit rate the market applies to NZX dividend payers, (b) zero credit for future value-accretive M&A, and (c) the fact that the historical multiple was earned by a 15%-EBITDA-margin, low-NCI business - today's enlarged group is 10%-margin with ~23% of profit leaking to minorities, so history's multiple overstates like-for-like value.

valuation_philosophy.earnings_basis: UNDERLYING, not reported. FY2025 reported NPATAS $101.0m includes ~$26.4m (group share; $40.6m pre-tax) of one-off, non-cash IFRS 3 step-acquisition remeasurement gains booked when previously-held 50% JV stakes (Fayman/FIG $23.9m, ANZ Exports $2.5m) were revalued on obtaining control. Anchoring on reported figures would be peak-earnings extrapolation; the model anchors on management Underlying (FY2025 Underlying EBITDA $137.6m, NPATAS $61.8m) and the year-1 build ties to FY2026 guidance (Underlying NPATAS $55-60m, raised 26-Aug-2026). Attributable unlevered NOPAT year 1 is $61.1m ~ guidance midpoint $57.5m plus after-tax borrowing interest - the model deliberately implies no more than ~$60m of near-term attributable earnings.
valuation_philosophy.growth_basis: Acquisition consolidation is separated from organic growth: year-1 revenue +55% is the full-year effect of the Sep-2025 acquisitions plus Esro control, not growth. The 54% headline FY2025 revenue CAGR-type figures are NOT extrapolated; organic growth thereafter is 4.5% fading to 2.5% (base). The lower-margin Edible Proteins trading base (H1-2026 gross margin 18.9% vs 31.3%) means revenue growth translates to earnings at a ~10% EBITDA margin, not the historical ~15%.
valuation_philosophy.market_gap: The DCF (weighted NZ$3.96) sits ~44% below the NZ$7.10 price, while the market itself is at 9.0x underlying EV/EBITDA and 16.8x underlying earnings - inside its own 10-year band. The disagreement is about the discount rate and M&A option value, not about FY2026 earnings: at the current price the base-case flows return ~7.5%/yr. Holders at $7.10 are being paid to underwrite (1) a single-digit discount rate on a weather-cyclical, NCI-leaky, integration-heavy earnings stream, and (2) continued value-accretive bolt-on M&A that a DCF of the existing business rightly excludes. The residual-income cross-check (warranted P/B 1.24x vs market 2.3x) says the same thing.
valuation_philosophy.risk_placement: Risk is charged once by design: recurring/systematic exposures (weather frequency, integration, FX) carry +1.5pp inside the 11.5% WACC applied to ALL scenarios; discrete severity (a Gabrielle-class FY2027 event, Esro deterioration) lives in the bear scenario at an elevated 25% weight. Terminal growth capped at 2.0-2.5% for a mature agribusiness; terminal value uses min(Gordon, 12x FCF) with Gordon binding at 10.7x.

guidance_tie_out.note: Model year-1 attributable NOPAT is unlevered (pre net borrowing interest, ~$3.6m after tax attributable), so $61.1m unlevered = ~$57.5m levered NPATAS = guidance midpoint. H1-2026 actual Underlying NPATAS was already $52.0m; H2 is seasonally small (Horticulture sells Mar-Aug) and carries the Esro drag.
